notes: ALTERNATE READING OF S.N. 24. The roster row is self-contradictory (company name 'Tjmaxx', domain homegoods.com). c24.json covers homegoods.com, which has no online catalogue at all. This file covers the actual T.J.Maxx e-commerce storefront, tjmaxx.tjx.com, which IS shoppable and does publish per-category counts. Pick one. TREE: taken from https://tjmaxx.tjx.com/store/resources/xml/categorySiteMap.xml (HTTP 200, 2,780 URLs) cross-checked against the site's own navigation feed. The complete Home department is Home > {Shop by Category, Shop by Room, Shop by Style}; only Shop by Category holds real product categories (Shop by Room / Shop by Style are roll-up buckets and were dropped, as were the seasonal buckets Back to Campus, Fall Decor and Halloween, and the out-of-scope Bed & Bath, Luggage & Travel, Pet, Stationery, Baskets & Storage, Blankets & Throws, Books, Curtains & Window Treatments, Rugs, Throw Pillows, Chairs & Seating, Tables, Cookbooks, Cookware & Bakeware, Cutlery & Flatware, Table & Kitchen Linens). There is no Clocks or Vases node anywhere on the site — the tree stops at the level extracted here, so 6 leaves is the true full extent of in-scope Home decor. COUNTS: the site's own first-party navigation feed, https://tjmaxx.tjx.com/store/sitewide/json/navMenuData.jsp (also served at /m/sitewide/json/navMenuData.jsp), which carries an itemCount for every node. This was NOT taken on trust: Decorative Accessories was independently rendered and its listing header read '809 items', its pagination read '1 / 5' with data-recsperpage=180 (ceil(809/180)=5), and the nav feed's itemCount for that same node is 809 — an exact three-way match. The desktop and mobile variants of the feed also return identical counts, so the mobile render is not a different population. The feed is likewise query-specific rather than static (the new-arrivals slice of Decorative Accessories returns 169, the clearance slice a different number again), which is the behaviour of a live count and not of an inflated catalogue field. CAVEAT the merge should be aware of: only Decorative Accessories could be verified against a rendered header; the other five counts rest on that one validated equivalence. ACCESS: TJX sits behind Akamai Bot Manager. Direct fetch with curl_cffi impersonate='chrome' returns the 'securityfailover' page on HTML; impersonate='safari17_2_ios' (mobile profile) returned full HTML for the first few requests, after which the IP was demoted to a hard deny and then to an unsolvable Akamai sec-cpt behavioural challenge that did not clear in 90 minutes of near-total silence. r.jina.ai returned Cloudflare challenges throughout (batch contention), translate.goog returned 403, WebFetch 403, and six public CORS/reader proxies failed. Pinning tjmaxx.tjx.com to the property's IPv6 Akamai edges (e81276.dscb/dsca/dscx.akamaiedge.net, e.g. 2600:140f:2e00::1701:f158) gave a fresh source IP but only ever reached the same JS challenge. The route that did work is that Akamai's bot rules only cover /store/shop/ and /m/shop/: robots.txt, /store/resources/xml/*.xml, /store/sitewide/json/navMenuData.jsp and /m/sitemap.jsp are all served unchallenged, and the nav feed carries the counts. SCOPE CALLS: Candles (149) dropped — TJ Maxx's candle assortment is predominantly scented/home-fragrance, excluded this batch. Plants & Planters (92) dropped as a mixed roll-up — it bundles artificial plants (excluded this batch) with decorative planters, has no sub-categories to split, and planters also appear inside Decorative Accessories. Outdoor Decor (58) dropped as garden/outdoor rather than home decoration. Decorative Accessories was kept but is a broad bucket: a 180-tile sample was roughly 71 decor objects, 39 picture frames, 38 books, 9 planters, 9 vases, 7 candle-related and 7 other, i.e. decor-dominant but with a books tail.
